results.title: Explainable AI Improves Breast MRI Cancer Detection
results.content:
Title: Explainable AI Improves Breast MRI Cancer Detection
##### AI Rebalances Breast Screening by Addres1. Radiologist reviewing mammography images on multiple monitors, representing breast imaging analysis and computer-assisted diagnosis. Technologist assisting patient during mammogram exam in a breast imaging clinic. Patient holding a pink ribbon in a mammography clinic, symbolising breast cancer awareness, screening and early detection. # Explainable AI Improves Breast MRI Cancer Detection. Breast MRI scan showing detailed tissue structure for cancer detection and diagnosis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers high sensitivity in detecting breast cancer, especially among women at elevated risk. A fully convolutional data description (FCDD) anomaly detection model has been developed to address these challenges, aiming to improve accuracy and explainability in both high- and low-prevalence breast MRI screening contexts. Most prior AI models for breast MRI have been evaluated using balanced datasets that do not reflect real-world prevalence, where malignant findings are rare. Anomaly detection offers a different approach by focusing on learning the characteristics of normal breast MRI scans, enabling better identification of abnormalities even when malignant cases are scarce. The FCDD model applies this principle to dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI data, generating pixel-level anomaly scores that can be aggregated into breast-level predictions. The model was developed using 9567 MRI examinations from 5026 patients collected over a decade, with two defined detection tasks: a balanced scenario including all cases and an imbalanced scenario reflecting realistic cancer prevalence. Imaging was processed into maximum intensity projections (MIPs), separated by breast and analysed using the FCDD model alongside comparison models, including binary cross-entropy (BCE) classification and hypersphere classification (HSC). The fully convolutional data description anomaly detection model represents a significant step forward in breast MRI screening, addressing both the performance drop seen in low-prevalence settings and the interpretability gap of prior AI approaches. While further validation in larger, lesion-annotated datasets and prospective clinical trials is needed, the model shows promise for enhancing breast MRI workflows, reducing false positives and improving diagnostic confidence. results.content:
Title: Explainable AI model finds breast tumors on MRI | AuntMinnie
# Explainable AI model finds breast tumors on MRI. An explainable AI model for cancer detection accurately outlined breast tumor location at breast MRI, according to research published July 15 in *Radiology*. "This model really excels in imbalanced datasets, which is what we have in the scenario of breast screening, where the event of a cancer being detected is fairly rare," corresponding author Savannah Partridge, PhD, from the University of Washington in Seattle, told *AuntMinnie*. (A) Diagram shows deep explainable anomaly detection at breast MRI. A maximum intensity projection (MIP) of a breast is passed to a fully convolutional neural network model trained using an explainable anomaly detection loss function (fully convolutional data description [FCDD]). Anomaly detection focuses on robustly learning the normal class and aims to identify abnormal cases accurately under these conditions.]()A method overview of the explainable AI model. (A) Diagram shows deep explainable anomaly detection at breast MRI. A maximum intensity projection (MIP) of a breast is passed to a fully convolutional neural network model trained using an explainable anomaly detection loss function (fully convolutional data description [FCDD]). Oviedo, Partridge, and colleagues developed their explainable AI model to detect breast cancer on MRI exams, aiming for the model to be effective in both high- and low-cancer-prevalence settings. It used 9,567 consecutive MRI exams to develop its explainable, fully convolutional data description anomaly detection model with the goal of finding malignancies on contrast-enhanced MRI scans. The researchers evaluated the model’s performance in three cohorts: grouped cross-validation for both balanced (20% malignant) and imbalanced (1.85% malignant) detection tasks, an internal independent test set (171 exams), and an external dataset. The findings add to the discussion on explainable AI models for detecting breast cancer at contrast-enhanced MRI, according to an accompanying editorial by Min Sun Bae, MD, PhD, from Korea University in Seoul and Sungwon Ham, PhD, from Korea University Ansan Hospital. ##### MRI-based model predicts treatment response in breast cancer patients. The debate between risk-based and annual mammography-based breast cancer screening continues, as recent research points to the former's benefits. results.title: How AI Reads Between the Lines to Reveal Personality Traits from Text
results.content: # How AI Reads Between the Lines to Reveal Personality Traits from Text. Researchers at the University of Barcelona show how AI models like BERT detect personality traits from text using explainable AI techniques. Categorized in:  AI News Science and Research. ## How AI Models Detect Personality Traits from Written Text. A research team at the University of Barcelona has demonstrated how artificial intelligence (AI) models can identify personality traits from written texts. The study involved experts from the Faculty of Psychology, the Institute of Neurosciences, and the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Barcelona. The researchers examined two advanced AI models, BERT and RoBERTa, to understand how they process text data to detect personality traits. Using text data from questionnaires labeled according to these models, the team applied explainable AI techniques to reveal which language patterns influence the models’ predictions. ### Related AI News for Science and Research.
